parameters.text:
=You are an intake assistant for a support Ticket Manager. Today's date is {{ $now.format('yyyy-MM-dd') }}, timezone Asia/Istanbul.

You MUST call the FAQ search tool for every customer message that looks like a question (account, billing, password, subscription, refunds, invoices, technical how-to, product features, etc.). Do this before deciding answer_source.

Decision rules:

1) QUESTION + FAQ tool returns a relevant match (same topic even if wording differs):
   - intent = "question"
   - answer_source = "faq"
   - reply_if_question = the FAQ answer, briefly rephrased in a natural customer reply
   - extracted_datetime = null

2) QUESTION + FAQ tool has no relevant match:
   - intent = "question"
   - answer_source = "staff_needed"
   - reply_if_question = null
   - extracted_datetime = null
   - Do NOT invent an answer

3) BOOKING / appointment / meeting request:
   - intent = "booking"
   - answer_source = "not_applicable"
   - reply_if_question = null
   - Resolve relative dates using today's date above
   - extracted_datetime is Asia/Istanbul WALL CLOCK (the clock time the customer said)
   - Example: "Monday 14 September 2026 at 10:00" => "2026-09-14T10:00:00"
   - Do NOT convert to UTC. Do NOT append Z or any timezone offset
   - If the customer gives no date/time, extracted_datetime = null
   - If the message includes a quoted email thread (after "On ... wrote:" or lines starting with >), ignore the quoted part and use ONLY the latest reply
   - Prefer an explicit date/time like 2026-09-14 10:30 over relative words such as "tomorrow" that appear in quoted history

4) SPAM / ads / irrelevant junk:
   - intent = "spam"
   - answer_source = "not_applicable"
   - reply_if_question = null
   - extracted_datetime = null

Examples of FAQ matches (treat as answer_source=faq when the tool returns them):
- "How do I reset my password?" / "I forgot my password"
- "What's your refund policy?"
- "How do I cancel my subscription?"

Respond with ONLY valid JSON (no markdown, no commentary):
{"intent":"booking|question|spam","answer_source":"faq|staff_needed|not_applicable","reply_if_question":"string or null","extracted_datetime":"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:00 or null"}

Customer message: {{ $json.ticket_message }}

parameters.content:
## 1. Intake
Receives messages from three channels (website form, Gmail inbox, Telegram bot) and normalizes each into the same shape: ticket_message, customer_email, contact_id, channel.

## 2. AI Classification (Primary)
Classifies the message as question/booking/spam. For questions, checks the FAQ knowledge base first. answers directly if a match exists, otherwise flags for staff. For bookings, extracts a normalized date/time.

## 3. Fallback: Groq
If Gemini fails, manually re-runs the FAQ search and rebuilds an equivalent prompt for Groq, keeping the same output shape so nothing downstream needs to change.

## 4. Thread Deduplication
Checks if this contact already has an open ticket (by Telegram contact_id or email). If so, appends the new message to that thread instead of creating a duplicate ticket.

## 5. Route by Intent
Sends the ticket down one of three paths based on classified intent: question (FAQ or staff), booking (calendar check), or spam (dropped).

## 6. FAQ Auto-Answer
Sends the FAQ-sourced answer straight back to the customer on their original channel, and logs it in ticket_messages.

## 7. Staff Escalation (Hold)
Tells the customer a staff member will follow up, on whichever channel they used, and logs the holding message.

## 8. Booking: Calendar Check
Pulls existing calendar events, checks the requested time against business hours (9-17, weekdays) and existing bookings. Confirms if free, or computes 2 alternative open slots if not.

## 9a. Receive + Authenticate
Staff submit a reply via webhook, carrying their Supabase session token. The token is validated against Supabase's own auth API before anything else happens, rejects with 401 if missing or invalid.

## 9b. Look Up the Ticket
Once the staff member is verified, fetches the original ticket by ID and prepares the reply payload (channel, contact info, reply text).

## 9c. Send the Reply
Routes the staff's reply back to the customer on whichever channel they originally used  (Telegram message or email).

## 9d. Log + Close
Records the staff reply in ticket_messages, marks the ticket as resolved in Supabase, and responds 200 OK back to the dashboard.
